### Problem

The review finds 3 of the 10 known bugs of its set (evals/review/, run 44976391834 on 2026-11-22). In 7 of the 10 it raises no finding at all in the file the bug is in ("no finding in the file", in most plays), so the misses are not near-misses on the line: the reviewer does not look closely at that file. It never blocks a clean case (10 of 10), so it has room to look harder. Today the prompt (claude-review.yml, step `claude`) asks for "every problem still open" with no method, and nothing in its answer shows which changed files it actually examined.

### Scope

- The review goes over every changed file of the diff, hunk by hunk, asking what each change can break (callers, other branches of the same logic, the tests that should cover it), and its structured answer says, for each changed file, that it was examined and what was checked; a changed file with no entry is a review that did not finish.
- The fixed review (scripts/fixed-review.py) and anything else that writes or reads the review's answer stay in step with its schema.
- The review evaluation (review-eval.yml) scores the change; its new baseline is committed with it.
- Tests, and docs/testing-and-quality.md, docs/workflows.md and the workflow header in step.

### Out of scope

- The review's model and effort per risk level (policy/review-policy.default.yml).
- The verification step's prompt.
- The cases of the review set.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given a pull request that changes several files, when the review answers, then its answer accounts for every changed file, and a missing one is treated as an unfinished review, not a clean one.
- C2: Given the review set, when review-eval.yml scores the change, then it finds more known bugs than the current baseline (3 of 10) and blocks no more clean cases than today (0 of 10).

### Criticality

Critical
